source.study: Machine learned daily life history classification using low frequency tracking data and automated modelling pipelines: application to North American waterfowl
source.narrative_from_source: Daily trajectory data from 131 tracked waterfowl across five species, with hourly GPS and same-month composited Landsat-8/Sentinel-2 MNDWI habitat covariates. 9334 augmented daily records used in the paper; the data release may have a different grain.
source.important_limit: Species identity intentionally withheld from publicly released modeling dataset; do not infer five species effects from individual identifiers or location.

scientific_question: Can the temporal water state experienced by a tracked animal be examined jointly with geographic displacement across consecutive dated GPS observations, and can static-site persistence be distinguished from state maintenance using a source-defined environmental reference?

data_gateway.stage: metadata, schema, filesize, source identity before ecological effects
field_required: contemporaneous habitat MNDWI at each location
source_quality_requirements: time-sorted repeated observations with unambiguous datetime, no row-order reconstructed identifiers
source MNDWI variable keyed to same acquired time or source-defined monthly window
sampled points are genuine GPS observations rather than just aggregated daily features
stop_if: MNDWI is a single dated static raster instead of source temporally linked to the fixes
Source download or metadata permission not available
Only daily mean/SD aggregate MNDWI without location-level join

outcome_restrictions.predeclare_only_after_source_schema: If point-level water-index and time/location are verified, freeze a distinct test of geographic displacement versus experienced water-index differences and at least one counterfactual comparison before computing effects.
blocked_claims: Site movement causally buffers experienced water state without a place-stationary environmental trajectory or accessibility-matched alternative
Artificially segmented hourly fixes are independent birds
Species-level phylogenetic generality from a dataset without species identifiers
New ecology from a supervised model's original feature engineering itself
